result.title: Lines Are Ideas: Visual Creativity Assessment in Hyperbolic Space
result.summary: Assessing human creativity from drawings provides a scalable way to evaluate human creative ability. However, existing approaches either rely on costly expert annotation or treat creativity as a single regression target, overlooking its underlying structure. Psychological theories have long emphasized that creativity emerges from balancing novelty and appropriateness. Motivated by this principle, we recast creativity as structured semantic deviation between paired drawings, where novelty measures the extent of departure from the original base sketch, and appropriateness determines whether such departures remain meaningful. This formulation naturally leads to a hyperbolic representation, in which novelty is quantified by geodesic distance and appropriateness is evaluated conditionally via a learned decision boundary, further regulated by an abstraction-conditioned adaptive constraint. Experiments on AuDrA-Drawings demonstrate state-of-the-art alignment with expert judgments and strong robustness under rater and task shifts. Beyond performance gains, our framework reveals an interpretable radial organization of creative variation, offering a principled geometric foundation for automatic creativity assessment.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将绘画创造力评估重构为成对草图间的「结构化语义偏离」：novelty 用双曲空间中的测地距离度量，appropriateness 用学习到的条件判别边界配合抽象度自适应约束判断，在 AuDrA-Drawings 上对齐专家评分并呈现可解释的径向组织。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「偏离幅度」与「偏离是否有意义」分离并用双曲几何量化的思路，可能为 latent 状态变化（如推理步间表示的位移与内容有效性）提供相似度度量上的启发，但与人或 VLM 的推理过程无直接关联，可供核查。
